rites.name: Graikok
rites.text: Graikok is the concept of the grain of stone that first condensed from the Singing in Kelolden, a low hum that settled into root and bedrock. It has no will of its own, only a pull that gathers loose sound into solid ground.

rites.name: Orasium
rites.text: A learned craft of tending the soil that opens the way to a tall grain-watch tower. It requires first gathering a rare iron stone from the ground.

rites.name: Ilovanoma
rites.text: Ilovanoma is the concept of a binding oath spoken at the Courts of Kelolden, when each council seat swears to hold a door open or shut. Its trials test whether a sworn word can bear weight, and its stone seals gather the small pressures of many promises into one lasting hinge.

rites.name: Cronuden
rites.text: Cronuden is a concept held in Kelolden's Courts, the idea that a sovereign's word can bind a grove to a single season. It is remembered as a quiet discipline of the first sovereign's councils rather than a weapon, shaping how the early kingdoms measured their promises.

rites.name: Ilyimannys
rites.text: Ilyimannys is a concept in Kelolden, a principle of measured judgment that the Courts of the Holy Age used to weigh oaths before the doors between worlds were raised. It was taught in temples as a discipline of patience rather than a power of its own. Its practitioners could sway a council or hold a sealed gate steady for a night.

rites.name: Elara
rites.text: Elara is a concept born in Kelolden during the Seeding, when the makers plant the Weave and quiet powers sleep across the Holy Age. She is remembered as an idea of flame and temple order, a name carried by the orders that tend the sacred hearths. Her influence was felt through ritual and craft rather than open force.

rites.name: Orolor
rites.text: Orolor is a concept of the Weave, the quiet web of threads the makers planted in Kelolden during the Seeding, when powers slept beneath the soil. In the Age of Sundering, when landfall broke the old bonds between peoples, Orolor was the idea that a single thread could be pulled to unravel a whole region of ties.

rites.name: Valilum
rites.text: A tireless craft of inner vigor that can be deepened without limit through study. Each stage of mastery grants its practitioner added resilience, and everyone begins with a fixed reserve of vitality.

rites.name: Morerdeld
rites.text: Morerdeld is a concept in the Kelolden record, born in the Walled Age, when holding walls, orders and churches stood against the wild lands. Its sense of duty was forged during the Holy Age, when flame and temple bound the orders together.

rites.name: Amasenum
rites.text: A late-age, endlessly consumed charge that labs burn to fuel one singular deepening art. Because it eases every other inquiry, it quietly speeds the progress of all learning.

rites.name: Ukalanuta
rites.text: Ukalanuta is an abstract concept in Kelolden, a notion of the branching of endings that the Library keeps on its shelves during the Holy Age of flame and temples. It is said to hold the shape of every choice not yet taken, and to be felt most strongly where orders gather.
